articles.title: Vietnam unlikely to meet 80% drug production target by 2030 - Healthcare Asia Magazine
articles.summary: Vietnam unlikely to meet 80% drug production target by 2030  Healthcare Asia Magazine
articles.full_text:
Local manufacturers remain concentrated in lower-value activities.
Vietnam is unlikely to produce enough pharmaceuticals domestically for 80% of local demand by 2030, due to heavy reliance on imported medicines and limited research and development (R&D) capabilities.
According to a BMI report, the country’s pharmaceutical imports are forecast to increase to $4.3b (VND118t) by 2030 from $3.2b (VND81.6t) in 2025.
The government approved a decision in October, outlining a pharmaceutical industry development strategy through 2030, with a longer-term vision for 2045.
It aims to strengthen pharmaceutical security by expanding active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) production, technology transfer, R&D investment and international collaboration.
By 2030, Vietnam aims to meet around 20% of domestic pharmaceutical raw material demand, establish at least two internationally accredited pharmaceutical R&D centres and achieve annual export growth of at least 10% for high-value pharmaceutical products.
Despite this, BMI said translating these targets into a competitive domestic industry would remain challenging.
The report noted that local manufacturers remain concentrated in lower-value activities such as generic drug formulation and packaging, whilst capabilities in complex formulations, biologics and innovative medicines remain limited.
Low R&D spending is another constraint as the country allocates just 0.4% of gross domestic product (GDP) to R&D, compared with 1.8% in Singapore, 1.2% in Thailand and 1.0% in Malaysia.
BMI said Vietnam's localisation agenda could increase pressure on multinational pharmaceutical companies to expand local investments, transfer technology and establish partnerships with domestic manufacturers.
However, attracting these investments will remain difficult amid workforce capability gaps, intellectual property concerns and high regulatory compliance costs.
The country's stronger economic outlook is expected to support pharmaceutical development spending. BMI raised its GDP growth forecast to 8.7% for 2026 and 7.9% for 2027, from previous estimates of 7.4% and 7.2%, respectively.
BMI expects pharmaceutical localisation to advance gradually, with self-sufficiency remaining a longer-term objective rather than an achievable outcome by 2030.

articles.title: Business, unusual: on engaging with the Myanmar junta - The Hindu
articles.summary: Business, unusual: on engaging with the Myanmar junta  The Hindu
articles.full_text:
Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away.
More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations.
The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance.
With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence.
The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity.
Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians.
Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory.
It also backed the January election.
Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India, Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states.
ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue.
Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point.
Meanwhile, U.
S.
officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September.
Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Indonesia eyes China's rare earth strategy to gain geopolitical leverage - Indonesia Business Post
articles.summary: Indonesia eyes China's rare earth strategy to gain geopolitical leverage  Indonesia Business Post
articles.full_text:
Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia says Indonesia should expand mineral processing to strengthen its bargaining power in global trade, following China’s use of rare earth industries as a geopolitical tool.
Indonesia should follow China’s approach to managing its natural resources by developing domestic processing industries, particularly for rare earth elements (REEs), to strengthen its economic and geopolitical position, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia said.
Speaking at the opening ceremony of Minerba Convex 2026 in Jakarta on Monday, November 2, 2026, Bahlil said China had demonstrated how mineral processing could become more than an economic strategy, serving as leverage in international negotiations.
He pointed to the ongoing strategic competition between China and the United States, in which rare earth products have become an important bargaining instrument because of their critical role in advanced technologies.
Bahlil argued that Indonesia should move beyond exporting raw minerals and instead develop domestic industries capable of processing its natural resources into higher-value products.
He said the approach was also consistent with Article 33 of the 1945 Constitution, which stipulates that natural resources must be controlled by the state and utilized for the greatest possible benefit of the population.
Nickel downstreaming offers a blueprint
Bahlil cited Indonesia's nickel downstreaming programme as evidence of the economic benefits of shifting away from raw material exports.
He said Indonesia's nickel export earnings stood at approximately US$3.3 billion (Rp55.1 trillion) in 2017–2019. Following the government's ban on nickel ore exports and the expansion of domestic processing facilities, the figure increased to between US$33 billion and US$34 billion (Rp550.6 trillion–Rp567.3 trillion) in 2023–2024.
The increase of roughly tenfold demonstrates how domestic processing can significantly raise the economic value captured from mineral resources, he said.
Indonesia has also developed an integrated electric vehicle battery ecosystem spanning mining, smelting, high-pressure acid leaching (HPAL) processing, precursor and cathode production, and battery cell manufacturing.
Bahlil said the country now has three battery factories, while domestically produced precursors and cathodes have also been supplied to the US market.
He believes this industrial development provides a foundation for expanding downstreaming beyond nickel, including into rare earth elements.
Mineral wealth amid global uncertainty
Bahlil also highlighted Indonesia's substantial mineral reserves, including the world's largest nickel reserves, as well as coal, bauxite, copper and tin. Indonesia is also the world's largest tin exporter, although its reserves rank below China's.
He argued that greater domestic processing capacity would help Indonesia strengthen its position in global supply chains while reducing its dependence on exporting unprocessed commodities.
The minister also warned that global economic and geopolitical uncertainty continues to affect Indonesia, even when the country is not directly involved in international conflicts. He cited rising global oil prices, which he said had exceeded US$100 per barrel, reaching approximately US$116 per barrel.
Bahlil compared Indonesia's continued reliance on raw material exports to the colonial-era trading model, in which domestic resources were shipped overseas for processing before finished products were sold back to the country.
He questioned whether Indonesia should continue following that pattern or instead retain more economic value through domestic industrial development.
For Bahlil, China's rare earth strategy and Indonesia's experience with nickel downstreaming demonstrate how control over processed mineral products can strengthen both economic returns and geopolitical bargaining power.

articles.title: FPT trials chip testing plant in northern Vietnam, targets 300 mln chips a year - Theinvestor
articles.summary: FPT trials chip testing plant in northern Vietnam, targets 300 mln chips a year  Theinvestor
articles.full_text:
Vietnamese technology group FPT Corporation has begun trial operations at its chip testing and packaging plant in the northern province of Bac Ninh, marking a step towards developing domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain.
The facility, operated by FPT Analysis Technologies JSC, has six production lines and a designed capacity of up to 300 million chips annually. Covering 1,600 square meters, it is located in Yen Phong II-C Industrial Park.
For chip testing, FPT uses automated test equipment (ATE) alongside handlers. The ATE system assesses chip functionality and performance, while handlers position components for testing and sort them according to whether they pass or fail.
The testing area is housed in a Class 10,000 cleanroom, equivalent to ISO Class 7, to control dust and other environmental factors.
FPT engineers also develop testing programs tailored to each chip design and its technical specifications. The process covers defining test parameters, setting testing conditions, and analyzing results.
The company is developing an artificial intelligence-powered platform to automate parts of test program development, from standardizing data and technical requirements to configuring tests and evaluating results.
Beyond functional testing, the facility will assess chip durability and reliability through tests under high temperatures, temperature cycling, and combined temperature and humidity conditions. Electrostatic discharge controls will also be used to reduce the risk of damage during handling.
FPT has assembled a team of semiconductor testing and packaging specialists and engineers, including personnel with years of experience at Intel's Vietnam facility. The team is responsible for developing technical procedures, operating equipment, and training employees.
During the initial phase, the plant will focus on chip functionality, quality and reliability testing, with the aim of serving semiconductor businesses in Vietnam and overseas. FPT plans to expand its reliability testing facilities to meet international requirements for testing and calibration laboratories.
The plant is expected to handle its first chip testing order for a South Korean partner, marking the start of its commercial service operations.
FPT also plans to use the facility as a practical training center. In cooperation with FPT Polytechnic College, the company will launch a pilot program in December to give students hands-on experience with chip testing equipment, production lines, and industrial processes.
Over the longer term, FPT aims to expand its advanced testing capabilities and develop chip packaging technology, broadening its role in the semiconductor supply chain.
The company has more than a decade of experience in semiconductor development and has designed products including power integrated circuits (Power ICs) and power management integrated circuits (PMICs). It is also pursuing research into AI-on-Edge system-on-chip (SoC) products.
Last year, FPT delivered its first batch of self-designed power chips to a Japanese partner, an initial step toward exporting its semiconductor products to Asian markets.
The new facility adds testing and packaging capabilities to FPT's existing chip design and workforce training activities. The company aims to build a more comprehensive semiconductor ecosystem and expand services for domestic and international customers, supporting Vietnam's efforts to move further into the global semiconductor value chain.

articles.title: Vietnam MarTech appoints new Chairman, unveils 5 strategic pillars to position Vietnam as a regional AI and Martech hub - Vietnam Economic Times
articles.summary: Vietnam MarTech appoints new Chairman, unveils 5 strategic pillars to position Vietnam as a regional AI and Martech hub  Vietnam Economic Times
articles.full_text:
Dr. Dinh Le Dat is the Co-founder & Chairman of Antsomi, Co-founder of the Customer Data Platform Institute Southeast Asia (CDP Institute SEA), and Co-founder of Vietnam MarTech. The organization has set a clear goal: to position Vietnam as one of Southeast Asia’s leading hubs for MarTech and Artificial Intelligence (AI) innovation, with a strong emphasis on Agentic AI.
Speaking at the Vietnam MarTech Day conference held on November 1, 2026, alongside updating advanced technology trends, Dr. Dinh Le Dat stressed the importance of community-building and enhancing practical MarTech adoption capabilities in Vietnam. He reaffirmed that Vietnam MarTech’s overarching priority is to elevate local MarTech talent to international standards. To realize this vision, the organization has established five strategic pillars.
The first pillar focuses on nurturing a workforce capable of seamlessly integrating business acumen, marketing knowledge, and technical skill set, rather than merely utilizing isolated tools. Next-generation practitioners must master customer data management, execute omnichannel marketing platforms, and measure campaign effectiveness. They are expected to shift from manual execution to strategic AI orchestrators managing workflow AI agents, while maintaining international-grade language proficiency for global work environments.
Vietnam MarTech has identified five core competence groups: Creative & Content, Advertising, and E-commerce; Customer Data & Customer Relationship Management (CRM/CDP); Marketing Automation (CEP) & Customer Journey Management; Analytics, Growth, and Strategy; and Digital Experience & AI Application.
To operationalize these competencies, the organization is launching three key initiatives. MarTech Academy will handle deep-dive technical and operational training. Leadership Masterclass is tailored for executives to develop strategic thinking and team management. Notably, the Talent Fellowship & MarTech Hackathon program targets students and young professionals, offering hands-on project practice and direct employment matchmaking.
The second pillar drives the integration of AI and Agentic AI into the entire marketing value chain, from problem selection and workflow design to performance control and evaluation.
Dr. Dat noted that the focus goes beyond generative AI for content creation; it lies in restructuring operating models, including data governance, quality control, and human-in-the-loop collaboration. MarTech professionals will set strategic objectives, supply input data, and determine critical human touchpoints. A guiding principle remains strict accountability, ensuring humans retain ultimate responsibility for AI-driven outcomes via access control, audit logging, and mandatory approvals at key operational stages.
Vietnam MarTech’s third pillar targets practical deployment and quantifiable business impact. Specifically, the organization assists enterprises in assessing their readiness prior to investment across five key dimensions: Business Objectives, Customer Data, Technology, Talent, and Operations & Measurement.
Deployment effectiveness will be quantified through core performance metrics, including marketing productivity, conversion rates, customer retention, customer lifetime value (CLV), and Return on Investment (ROI). Global Vietnamese experts will also be mobilized under this pillar to share battle-tested insights and benchmark international best practices for the local ecosystem.
Under the fourth pillar, Vietnam MarTech aims to foster a collaborative ecosystem by proactively bridging businesses, brands, universities, research institutes, and international partners to broaden knowledge access.
This strategy will be executed via three landmark programs. The MarTech Industry - University Partnership program accelerates corporate-academic collaboration in curriculum co-development and internship placements. The SEA MarTech Exchange serves as a cross-border networking hub for regional MarTech experts and organizations to exchange industry expertise. Finally, the annual Vietnam MarTech Day held on November 1 serves as the largest flagship gathering to connect the community, release industry research, and promote trade partnerships.
The fifth pillar aims to build a standardized reference system, equipping enterprises with scientific criteria for investment decisions while helping practitioners benchmark and validate their expertise.
Vietnam MarTech commits to strict research transparency, independence from sponsored content, authorized data utilization, and respect for intellectual property rights, thereby laying a trustworthy foundation for the market.
Sharing his long-term vision, Dr. Dinh Le Dat highlighted that as Agentic AI becomes deeply embedded in marketing, Vietnam’s key opportunity lies in building systems that harmonize human intelligence, data assets, and AI execution capabilities. This will be the key to transforming marketing from a mere promotional support function into a core growth engine for the entire enterprise.
Initiated in 2018 and officially launched on November 1, 2023, Vietnam MarTech became a strategic member of the Asia AdMarCom Alliance in July 2026, deepening ties with premier regional advertising and tech associations. Between 2018 and 2026, the network connected over 50,000 marketers and hosted 20 deep-dive national seminars.
Graduating with honors and earning his Ph.D. in Big Data & Semantic Web from Lomonosov Moscow State University (Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics), Dr. Dinh Le Dat is the Co-founder & Chairman of Antsomi, Co-founder of CDP Institute SEA, Co-founder of Vietnam MarTech, and an advisor/expert for the Vietnam E-commerce Association (VECOM). He previously served as Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at FPT Online and as a strategic advisor on MarTech and customer data for major Retail and F&B conglomerates across Vietnam and the ASEAN region. On the global stage, he was the sole Southeast Asian representative speaking at MarTech World Forum 2024 in Melbourne, Australia. He also served as the sole Vietnamese representative presenting at ASIA Pacific Media Forum 2024 in Bali, Indonesia and d-Conference 2024 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, as well as the sole Vietnamese speaker on Customer Data Platforms at Big Data World Asia Conference 2022 in Singapore.

articles.title: Malaysia halal safeguards questioned after 6.5 tonnes of chicken seized - The Straits Times
articles.summary: Malaysia halal safeguards questioned after 6.5 tonnes of chicken seized  The Straits TimesMalaysia’s halal chicken scandal exposes hygiene breaches at filthy plant  South China Morning PostJais probing ownership of raided Puchong poultry plant  Free Malaysia TodayOnly four slaughterhouses in KL hold Jakim halal certification  NST OnlineSlaughterhouse operators encouraged to apply for Malaysia Halal Certification  The Malaysian Reserve
articles.full_text:
Why electric stunning of chickens at a Selangor slaughterhouse triggered halal concerns
AI generated
KUALA LUMPUR – A raid at a chicken slaughterhouse in Selangor that uncovered more than 6.5 tonnes of poultry suspected of being slaughtered in violation of Islamic requirements has raised concerns about the integrity of Malaysia’s halal supply chain.
Selangor Menteri Besar Amirudin Shari on Nov 2 called for firm action, including prosecution, against slaughterhouses and poultry processing facilities found to have broken the law.
He said halal certification bodies and the local authorities needed to work together to ensure regular monitoring of sensitive operations such as slaughterhouses.
“Regular inspections must be carried out so that we can ensure sensitive operations are conducted according to the procedures and requirements that have been set,” he was quoted as saying by The Star daily.
Matters concerning halal certification and enforcement are sensitive in multiracial Malaysia and have the potential to cause racial tensions.
The discovery is particularly troubling because the facility in Puchong reportedly operated for about 20 years without valid halal certification, despite prior notices and reminders from the authorities.
The scale of the operation has also drawn attention.
The facility could process more than 40,000 chickens a day, and the poultry was believed to have been distributed to grocery shops, restaurants and other businesses in areas in the Klang Valley including Puchong, Putrajaya, Damansara, Cheras and Bangi.
There is no indication that the Puchong facility supplied Singapore or that any of the seized poultry was destined for the Singapore market.
The case has prompted concerns over how such an operation could continue for so long and how a facility allegedly operating outside regulatory requirements could process and distribute poultry on such a scale.
It also puts the effectiveness of enforcement and monitoring under scrutiny, at a time when Malaysia is seeking to strengthen its position as a leading global halal hub, across not just food and beverages but also pharmaceuticals, fashion and finance.
Initial investigations suggested that the chickens had been electrically stunned using a water-bath method, with the voltage allegedly so far above the prescribed limit that some birds died before slaughter.
“This is a matter of grave concern as the slaughtering method is one of the key elements in determining the halal status of a chicken product,” Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director (Operations) Muhammad Abdul Halim was quoted as saying by the Bernama news agency.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council chairman Salehuddin Saidin said the authorities had raised the possibility that the poultry might have been supplied to restaurants owned by Muslims.
The premises were raided in the early hours of Oct 30 under Ops Taring Chiller, a joint operation involving the police, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM), the Department of Environment and the Petaling District Health Office.
JAKIM said the factory was suspected of slaughtering, processing and distributing fresh chicken without local authority permits and approvals. It also did not hold a halal certificate.
Malaysia has positioned its halal certification system as a competitive advantage in attracting investment, expanding exports and establishing the country as an international reference point for halal standards.
The implications extend beyond Malaysia’s domestic market.
The country is a key supplier of poultry to neighbouring Singapore, making the credibility of its halal certification and regulatory oversight relevant to regional trade.
According to Observatory of Economic Complexity trade data, Malaysia exported around RM56 million (S$17.6 million) worth of poultry meat to Singapore between September 2025 and August 2026.
Malaysia’s halal exports grew 10.9% to RM68.52 billion in 2025, up from RM61.79 billion in 2024, with China as the largest destination.
The incident has also revived concerns about Malaysia’s track record in enforcing halal standards, particularly after a meat cartel scandal in 2020, in which investigations found that non-halal meat had been passed off as halal using fake logos and documentation.
Research director at IMAN Research, Aziff Azuddin, said the latest case could further erode public confidence in the country’s halal certification system, even as Malaysia continues to enjoy a strong international reputation in the sector.
Malaysia’s halal trademark is registered and recognised in nearly 50 countries, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in September 2025.
The Malaysia International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) 2026, a key halal exhibition held from Sept 23 to 26, recorded total sales of RM6.78 billion, up 12% from 2025.
“Instances like this chicken factory issue will affect how Malaysians themselves see and trust the halal certification,” he told The Straits Times.
He said the case pointed to wider concerns about enforcement.
“The fact that the factory operated for more than two decades and was emboldened to slaughter the chickens in a non-syariah compliant method could only mean that there was a lack of monitoring,” he said.
Syaza Shukri, a political analyst at the International Islamic University Malaysia, said the incident could dent Malaysia’s reputation for maintaining stringent halal standards, but noted that the raid and earlier notices issued by the authorities could also indicate that enforcement agencies were taking steps to ensure compliance.
She said the case could prompt wider questions about whether similar breaches had occurred elsewhere and the status of poultry already consumed by the public.
“We have a reputation for supposedly strict halal standards, and yet this could (still) happen,” she told ST.
She added that the authorities would need to address these concerns.
“There will be a lot of questions. What matters is whether they can be answered and more importantly, whether action is taken to ensure it doesn’t happen again.”
The incident has also sparked an outcry on social media, with both Muslim and non-Muslim consumers expressing dismay over the alleged breaches.
A Threads user, maryamsky9, questioned how such an incident could happen in Malaysia, which is known for its halal standards.
“This is bad. This is not a small issue. As far as I know, Malaysia really takes care of ‘halal’. How could this happen?” the user wrote.
On X, user Choen Lee posted on Nov 2: “OK this is disgusting. It’s not even about halal or not.”
Another Threads user, shinchan27324, wrote: “As a non muslim i also feel disgusted.”
The facility has been ordered to close for two weeks while investigations are carried out.

articles.title: US courts Myanmar to spur peace talks and tap rare earths over China - Chosunbiz
articles.summary: US courts Myanmar to spur peace talks and tap rare earths over China  Chosunbiz
articles.full_text:
The United States is reengaging with Myanmar's military, which it sought to isolate in the international community after the 2021 military coup. The aim is to push peace talks to end the civil war while also securing a chance to access Myanmar's abundant rare earth resources. As Myanmar's rare earths are mainly exported to China, Washington is seen as trying to use peace negotiations to lay the groundwork for U.S. corporations to enter.
According to Reuters on the 2nd (local time), a Myanmar country strategy document recently released by the U.S. State Department outlines a plan to expand U.S. influence and secure economic benefits through peace negotiations. Approved on Aug. 31, the document sets goals to support talks involving multiple armed groups in Myanmar while expanding business opportunities for U.S. corporations.
Since Myanmar's military seized power in a 2021 coup, the United States has imposed sanctions on military leaders and related corporations and pushed for international isolation. Min Aung Hlaing, who led the coup, is now heading a civilian government backed by the military.
Since the coup, a civil war has continued among the military, pro-democracy forces, and ethnic armed groups. According to the United Nations (UN), about 100,000 people have been killed and more than 3.5 million have fled. Some ethnic armed groups have fought the military for decades to secure autonomy.
◇ Shift from sanctions and isolation to pragmatic diplomacy
Economic interests tied to securing rare earths are cited as the backdrop for the Trump administration's renewed contact with Myanmar's military. Rare earths are critical minerals used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, and advanced weapons. The United States is working to diversify supply chains to reduce dependence on China, which dominates rare earth production and processing.
Myanmar has substantial rare earth deposits, but major mines are concentrated in regions destabilized by the civil war. To access these resources, the United States must consider relations not only with Myanmar's government but also with ethnic armed groups that control mining areas. Currently, Myanmar's rare earths are mainly exported to China.
Amid these interests, the United States has resumed contact with Myanmar's military side. Reuters reported last month that Washington held closed-door talks with the government backed by the Myanmar military. Michael Vans, Deputy Minister who leads the State Department's Bureau of Intelligence and Research, took part in a September meeting in Naypyitaw with President Min Aung Hlaing. The talks covered the release of an American businessman and a crackdown on online scam networks. The two sides later held additional talks in Tokyo, Japan.
However, the United States has not fully lifted sanctions on Myanmar's military. Financial sanctions on President Min Aung Hlaing and individuals and corporations linked to the military remain in place. The Trump administration removed some Myanmar nationals and corporations from the sanctions list, but much of the existing regime remains.
◇ The U.S. economic calculus behind the peace talks
Washington is linking its rare earth push to Myanmar's peace talks. According to the State Department's strategy document, the United States plans to support cease-fire negotiations that could lead to a sustainable peace accord by 2030. To that end, it set a goal of holding at least three rounds of multilateral consultations to produce concrete agreements or policy proposals on fiscal federalism and the delineation of territorial boundaries.
Fiscal federalism refers to a system that divides fiscal authority between central and local governments. The delineation of territorial boundaries concerns setting each region's jurisdiction. Both issues are key in Myanmar, where various armed groups are active, as they can affect resource development and regional governance.
The State Department strategy document states that these consultations will create opportunities to access Myanmar's abundant rare earth resources. The idea is to ease conflicts between the military and ethnic armed groups to reduce uncertainty in resource development and create conditions for U.S. corporations to enter.
The United States is also working to expand trade with Myanmar. The State Department strategy document includes a plan to increase U.S. exports to Myanmar to reduce the trade deficit. The U.S. Embassy in Myanmar set a goal of securing at least three commercial or investment contracts worth more than $5 million (about 6.7 billion won) each for U.S. corporations.
Beyond economic interests, responding to online scam crimes targeting Americans is also a key task. The United States plans to work with Myanmar authorities to crack down on local scam networks while also pushing to repatriate Myanmar nationals staying in the United States.
Still, it is uncertain whether Washington's plan will actually lead to securing rare earths. Even if dialogue with the military has resumed, that does not mean local cooperation and investment conditions needed for mine development are in place. The State Department strategy document also does not lay out concrete ways to resolve investment constraints on corporations under existing sanctions.
For the United States to secure rare earths in Myanmar, it must go beyond diplomatic contact and create an environment where resource development is possible. Whether the United States, which has extended a hand to Myanmar through peace talks, can bring substantive change to the China-centric rare earth supply chain will be a key question going forward.

articles.full_text:
Shuhaily was charged last month with two counts of assaulting two policemen at KLIA in September. He claimed trial to both charges.
Speaking in the Dewan Rakyat, Anwar rejected suggestions that the charges against Shuhaily were politically motivated, saying the government had no reason to act against an officer whose career it helped revive.
He said neither he nor home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail interfered in the matter, adding that decisions on whether to prosecute rested with the Attorney-General’s Chambers.
“We brought him back because of his performance. I remember bringing him from Penang to Kuala Lumpur before he was promoted,” he said during Prime Minister’s Question Time.
“Personally, I sympathise with him. But when there is an allegation, whether from the public or the police, it must be investigated.”
Anwar was responding to Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau), who questioned the government’s decision to return Shuhaily to the police force, saying he should be allowed to continue heading the border agency.
Shahidan praised Shuhaily’s performance and asked why action was being taken against an officer whom he described as one of the country’s best.
Shuhaily, 54, pleaded not guilty at the Sepang magistrates’ court on Oct 21 to two charges of causing hurt to two policemen at KLIA on Sept 28.
Saifuddin announced on Oct 29 that Shuhaily would be returned to the police force. However, Shuhaily resumed his duties at AKPS yesterday, chairing a meeting with the agency’s senior officers.
Inspector-General of Police Khalid Ismail earlier said that Shuhaily’s appointment could only be terminated prematurely with the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. He also said legal advice was being sought before the officer’s return to the police force could be finalised.
Shuhaily joined the police force in 1998 and began his career in the Special Branch.
He later held several senior intelligence and operational positions, including that of police attaché in Washington DC, before serving as district police chief, Penang police chief and Kuala Lumpur police chief.
He was appointed Bukit Aman criminal investigation department director in August 2023 and seconded to AKPS as its director-general in July 2025.

articles.title: From Haier and Toyota to Samsung: What lessons can Vietnamese businesses learn to expand globally? - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: From Haier and Toyota to Samsung: What lessons can Vietnamese businesses learn to expand globally?  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Quality, technology, and long-term strategies.
 At the Vietnam Export Promotion Forum 2026, themed "Go Global – Together with Businesses to Reach the World," held on November 4th in Hanoi, Mr. Vu Ba Phu, Director of the Trade Promotion Department (Ministry of Industry and Trade), recounted the development journeys of three major global brands: Haier (China), Toyota (Japan), and Samsung ( Korea ), thereby emphasizing the lessons for Vietnamese businesses on their path to internationalization.
 According to Mr. Vu Ba Phu, in the mid-1980s, Haier was just a small refrigerator factory in Qingdao ( China ), operating at a loss and producing low-quality products. In 1985, after discovering 76 defective refrigerators in the warehouse, the company's leadership ordered workers to smash all of them with hammers.
 This seemingly costly decision reflects Haier's consistent philosophy on quality. The company is not in a hurry to expand its market but focuses on building core competencies, using quality and reputation domestically as a foundation before developing scale, products, and management capabilities.
 In 1999, Haier built its first factory in South Carolina (USA), shifting from exporting to manufacturing directly in its target market. In 2016, the group further expanded its international position through the acquisition of GE's home appliance business for approximately $5.4 billion. 
 According to Mr. Phu, the lesson from Haier is that quality builds the foundation, while acquiring businesses with established brands and distribution systems can shorten the path to building a position in the international market.
 For Toyota, the journey to expand globally wasn't always smooth sailing. In 1957, the first Toyota Crowns were exported to the United States, but they were a near failure due to their small size, low power, and unsuitability for the traffic and highway conditions in that market. The engine overheated easily, and the cramped interior space resulted in low sales and high maintenance and repair costs.
 Instead of giving up, Toyota sent personnel to study the market, improve products, and perfect its lean manufacturing methods. The Kaizen method later became one of the manufacturing management principles adopted by many businesses around the world.
 Alongside exports, Toyota gradually built its overseas production capacity, expanding its manufacturing, engineering, and distribution networks in key markets. In 1989, the Lexus brand was launched, directly competing with European luxury car brands.
 From this story, Mr. Phu emphasized that businesses cannot understand the market only from a distance. Initial failures only truly become failures if businesses do not learn from them and adjust their strategies.
 Meanwhile, Samsung started by producing black and white televisions after Samsung Electronics was founded in 1969. The company collaborated with Japanese and German partners to learn technology, gradually expanding exports to South America and Panama.
 In 1983, Samsung made a significant investment in semiconductor memory chips, despite lagging behind many competitors. By 1993, in Frankfurt, the company's chairman called for a complete overhaul, shifting the focus from quantity to quality and branding.
 Today, Samsung has become one of the world's leading technology brands and a major semiconductor chip manufacturer. Vietnam is also an important production base for the group.
 The lesson from Samsung is that mass-market products can be a starting point, but to go far, businesses must dare to invest in long-term technological capabilities.
 "These three stories show that despite different starting points and paths, businesses share a common development logic. That is, building a foundation of quality, production capacity, management, and competitive products; accessing international markets to find customers and learn standards. Then, upgrading from simple processing, assembly, and export to developing technology, branding, and distribution systems. Global status is not a starting point but the result of a strategic, persistent, and long-term development journey," Mr. Phu shared.
 Small businesses also have the opportunity to go global.
 Not only businesses, but the State also plays a crucial role in the internationalization process. According to Mr. Vu Ba Phu, China focuses on strategic direction and resource mobilization; Japan concentrates on providing information, connecting partners, and minimizing risks; while South Korea supports businesses at each stage of development, linking them to an ecosystem for international trade promotion and distribution. 
 Vietnamese businesses showcase their products at Foodexpo 2025.
 The common feature of these models is that the State does not replace businesses but supports them in reducing costs and risks, and shortening the time to access foreign markets.
 For Vietnam, after nearly 40 years of reform, the export base has been strengthened with a network of 18 free trade agreements. By October 2026, total import and export turnover exceeded 1 trillion USD.
 Several Vietnamese businesses have also demonstrated their international capabilities. Viettel currently invests in 10 overseas markets, leading the market share in 7 of them, and is expected to achieve international revenue of approximately US$3.3 billion by 2025. FPT is projected to generate over VND 35 trillion in revenue from overseas IT services by 2025, with new contract values estimated at around US$1.5 billion.
 However, the international market is increasingly demanding higher quality, standards, green development, and traceability. Besides exports, businesses also have opportunities to expand through overseas distribution, cross-border digital trade, and international investment.
 In this context, the Go Global program, developed by the Ministry of Industry and Trade, aims to create an ecosystem to support the internationalization of businesses. By 2027, the program is expected to focus on three main tasks: implementing the Go Global Index, operating the Go Global Platform to connect businesses with support resources, and organizing training and consulting according to a unified program framework.
 The head of the Trade Promotion Department believes that businesses need to proactively develop internationalization strategies, invest in improving capabilities, and clearly define target markets. In particular, businesses should not wait until they are large enough to consider expanding abroad.
 In fact, Vietnam has startups in the field of manufacturing drones, drone motors, and drone propulsion systems that have proactively participated in international trade fairs. According to information shared by Mr. Phu from assessment organizations, Vietnam currently ranks second in the world, after China, in drone motor production.
 This shows that small and newly established businesses still have opportunities to access international markets if they have suitable products and capabilities.
 For localities and associations, the Director of the Trade Promotion Department suggested proactively identifying, preparing, and supporting potential businesses. Domestic and international partners are also expected to participate in connecting expertise, markets, and resources to create practical support.
 "Go Global is not the destination of an event, but a long-term development journey. The measure of the program's success is how many businesses actually take another step on their journey to reach the world," Mr. Phu emphasized.

articles.title: Bac Ninh aims to enhance the global competitiveness of its businesses. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Bac Ninh aims to enhance the global competitiveness of its businesses.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
With export turnover estimated at US$101.30 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, Bac Ninh continues to affirm its position as a major production and export center. However, to reach the global market, the locality has identified the focus not only on increasing export turnover but also on enhancing competitiveness, developing domestic enterprises, and participating more deeply in international value chains.
Creating momentum to expand into international markets.
At the Vietnam Export Promotion Forum 2026, organized by the Ministry of Industry and Trade , with the theme "Go Global - Together with businesses to reach the world," Mr. Nguyen The Thi, Deputy Director of the Department of Industry and Trade of Bac Ninh city, shared orientations and solutions to support businesses in enhancing their competitiveness, expanding markets, and gradually participating more deeply in the global supply chain.
Tìm hiểu lịch sử
According to estimates, in the first 10 months of 2026, Bac Ninh city's export turnover reached approximately US$101.30 billion, an increase of 32.51% compared to the same period last year; import turnover reached approximately US$103.40 billion, an increase of 43.81%. The total import and export turnover reached over US$204.70 billion.
These figures reflect the large scale of trade and the deep integration of Bac Ninh's economy with international markets and partners. Along with production and logistics infrastructure, the banking, finance, and international payment systems are also contributing to supporting the production, business, and integration of enterprises.
According to reports from the banking sector, as of September 30, 2026, total mobilized capital reached VND 458,657 billion, and total outstanding loans were estimated at VND 419,017 billion. In the first nine months of the year, foreign exchange trading volume reached approximately USD 10 billion, and import and export payment volume through banks reached approximately USD 37.8 billion.
However, Bac Ninh also recognizes that a large scale of import and export does not necessarily equate to high competitiveness and self-reliance. Export activities are still mainly concentrated on a few groups of electronic goods and components; there is still much room for domestic enterprises to directly participate in high value-added stages, develop brands, and build international distribution networks.
Furthermore, a segment of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) still face difficulties in terms of capital, market information, human resources, international standards, and risk management. Therefore, the requirement for localities is not only to promote export growth in quantity but also to improve the quality, value, and sustainability of export activities.
The Go Global program puts businesses at the center.
Following the central government's guidelines, especially the Program for Reaching International Markets in the period 2026-2030 approved by the Prime Minister , Bac Ninh has issued its own local program for reaching international markets in the period 2026-2030 under Decision No. 1098/QD-UBND dated August 19, 2026.
The overarching principle of the program is to place businesses at the center, with the State playing a facilitating role, supporting connections and removing barriers; the effectiveness of enhancing competitiveness, expanding markets, and participating in value chains for businesses is determined as the measure of implementation.
By 2030, Bac Ninh aims to organize or integrate at least 10 training and information dissemination activities, creating access opportunities for at least 1,000 businesses and production and business entities; provide in-depth consulting for at least 50 businesses and cooperatives; and support capacity building for at least 20 businesses with the potential to participate in the supply chain.
You may also like
At the same time, the city aims to support 50 to 100 businesses, cooperatives, and production and business entities in accessing digital platforms and cross-border e-commerce. These targets must be implemented with a focus on tangible results, not just on the quantity of activities.
In practice, localities have actively implemented activities to support businesses in taking advantage of free trade agreements (FTAs), providing guidance on rules of origin, resolving difficulties in implementing procedures, and expanding trade connections.
From December 10, 2025 to September 30, 2026, the Department of Industry and Trade issued 15,140 Certificates of Origin (C/O), facilitating businesses in meeting market requirements and exploiting preferential treatment from FTAs. Bac Ninh also gradually implemented an FTA utilization ecosystem, strengthening coordination between management agencies, support organizations, and the business community.
Notably, on October 10, 2026, the "Go Global Bac Ninh 2026" Forum, themed "Capacity Building - Supply Chain Connection - Market Development," was held in the city, attracting approximately 300 delegates representing management agencies, associations, experts, domestic businesses, FDI enterprises, and partners.
Activities focus on enhancing the capacity of domestic manufacturing enterprises, directly connecting them with the needs of buyers and upstream businesses. Along with the industrial sector, Bac Ninh continues to prioritize market promotion for agricultural products, especially lychees, processed products, OCOP products, and handicraft products with export potential.
Five groups of solutions to elevate businesses in the international market.
To realize its goal of expanding into the global market, Bac Ninh has identified five key tasks, focusing on improving the business environment, enhancing enterprise capacity, and building a comprehensive support ecosystem.
First and foremost, the city continues to build a favorable and transparent business environment, reducing costs and risks for businesses. The focus is on reforming administrative procedures, promoting digital transformation in serving businesses; strengthening dialogue and support regarding import and export, rules of origin, technical standards, intellectual property protection, logistics, and related procedures.
In addition, localities proactively provide information and warnings on trade defense, origin fraud, policy changes, and requirements related to the environment, labor, and sustainable development.
Another important task is to promote linkages between domestic businesses and FDI enterprises, gradually improving the position of Bac Ninh businesses in the global supply chain. The city focuses on surveying the needs of corporations, manufacturers, and buyers; selecting potential domestic businesses to support in assessing supplier capabilities, technological innovation, quality improvement, management refinement, and human resource training.
Following this direction, networking activities should not be limited to meetings and information exchange, but should be continuously monitored through bid submissions, supplier evaluation processes, improvement plans, and the potential for long-term partnerships. This is considered a practical approach to increasing the localization rate, the quality of growth, and the self-reliance of the city's economy.
Regarding market development, Bac Ninh will coordinate with the Ministry of Industry and Trade and the system of Vietnamese trade offices abroad to connect market information, key businesses, distributors, and cross-border e-commerce channels. For industrial products, the focus will be on improving supply capacity, quality standards, and the ability to participate in the value chain. For agricultural products, processed foods, OCOP products, and handicraft products, export support will be linked to the entire process from raw material areas, traceability, packaging, preservation, processing to brand building and distribution channels.
You may also like
In addition, the city focuses on promoting the role of the banking system and financial institutions in supporting businesses to access credit, trade finance, guarantees, international payments, green finance, and other legitimate financial services; while also disseminating knowledge on foreign exchange management, payment risk prevention, and fraud identification in cross-border transactions.
Ultimately, Bac Ninh aims to build a Go Global business support ecosystem with the participation of the Ministry of Industry and Trade, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Science and Technology, the Ministry of Agriculture , Customs, banks, associations, training institutions, and consulting organizations. The effectiveness of the program will be measured not only by the number of conferences held but also by the number of more mature businesses, the number of cooperation opportunities opened up, and the ability to realize those opportunities.
From the local perspective, the People's Committee of Bac Ninh City proposed that the Ministry of Industry and Trade continue to play a coordinating role in the Go Global Program nationwide; enhance the sharing of market information and buyer data, and provide early warnings of trade barriers; and support the locality in connecting with the system of Vietnamese Trade Offices abroad and the Go Global Partner Network.
At the same time, the city proposed focusing on organizing in-depth consulting programs and connecting suppliers by industry, especially in electronics, semiconductors, mechanics, supporting industries, agricultural products, and processed foods, in line with the strengths and needs of businesses in Bac Ninh.

articles.title: Vietnam central bank eases long-term funding constraints, boosting stock market hopes - Theinvestor
articles.summary: Vietnam central bank eases long-term funding constraints, boosting stock market hopes  Theinvestor
articles.full_text:
The State Bank of Vietnam's (SBV) planned liquidity injection of up to $2 billion through a six-month foreign exchange swap facility is expected to ease pressure on the banking system, improve investor sentiment and support the stock market.
The SBV on Wednesday announced plans to conduct a 182-day foreign exchange swap (FX Swap) operation on Friday, November 6, with a maximum size of $2 billion.
Under the arrangement, the central bank will buy U.S. dollars at a spot exchange rate of VND24,399 per dollar and sell them back at a forward rate of VND24,704 per dollar. The transaction value date is expected to be November 9, 2026, with maturity scheduled for May 10, 2027.
Eligible participants include credit institutions and foreign bank branches with outstanding medium- and long-term foreign loans or international bonds carrying a remaining maturity of at least 12 months. Each bank may register for up to 80% of the operation's total size, subject to the limit of its eligible outstanding foreign currency debt.
Through the operation, eligible banks can temporarily convert their U.S. dollar holdings into Vietnamese dong to supplement liquidity. The maximum amount of VND liquidity potentially injected into the system is estimated at VND48,798 billion ($1.9 billion).
Notably, the latest FX swap operation has a significantly longer maturity than previous interventions. According to brokerage VPS Securities JSC, the SBV has conducted several FX swap operations since the beginning of 2026, typically with maturities ranging from three to 21 days and maximum sizes of $1 billion to $2 billion.
In September alone, the central bank conducted two FX swap operations: a $2 billion facility with a seven-day maturity on September 21 and a $1 billion facility with a three-day maturity on September 28.
Extending the maturity to 182 days therefore marks a notable shift in the SBV's approach to liquidity management.
According to a flash report released on Wednesday, VPS said the SBV was proactively supporting VND liquidity amid rising funding demand across the banking system. With a maximum size of $2 billion, the FX swap operation could help ease liquidity pressures and cool interbank interest rates.
More importantly, the extension of the swap maturity to 182 days would allow banks to maintain more stable funding sources over a longer period, reducing the need to repeatedly roll over funding and limiting the risk of short-term liquidity shortages.
As pressure on the interbank funding market eases, banks may also have less need to compete aggressively for deposits from households and businesses, potentially curbing upward pressure on deposit rates in the domestic deposit market, known as Market 1.
However, VPS cautioned that the exchange rate spread of VND305 per dollar, equivalent to approximately 2.51% per year, does not fully reflect the operation's overall funding costs, as these also depend on the initial cost of raising U.S. dollar funding.
Consequently, the benefits for funding costs and net interest margins (NIM) are likely to vary among banks rather than translate into uniform improvements across the sector.
Additional tailwinds for the stock market
The SBV's move to strengthen liquidity support is also expected to have positive implications for the stock market. According to VPS, additional liquidity in the banking system and expectations of lower interbank interest rates could improve investor sentiment, ease concerns over rising borrowing costs, and support equity valuations.
Sectors particularly sensitive to interest rate movements, including securities, real estate and banking, could stand to benefit.
A stable interest rate environment helps ease companies' funding cost pressures while limiting the relative attractiveness of fixed-income investment products compared with equities.
For securities firms, improved market liquidity could support brokerage activities, margin lending and proprietary trading. Real estate companies, meanwhile, could benefit if interest rate pressures remain under control, helping reduce financing costs and improve homebuyers' access to credit.
For banks, the additional liquidity could ease funding balance pressures and reduce competition for deposits. However, the extent of the benefits will depend on each institution's funding structure, its ability to participate in the FX swap operation and its actual cost of capital.
Nevertheless, VPS noted that the impact of the FX swap operation on the stock market would be largely indirect. Its actual influence on overall interest rates will depend on the volume of transactions conducted, the cost of raising U.S. dollar funding and the SBV's liquidity management through other instruments.
The latest FX swap operation should also be viewed primarily as a targeted liquidity management measure rather than a signal that the central bank is shifting towards broad-based monetary easing.
As the SBV is obliged to sell the U.S. dollars back when the contracts mature in May 2027, the VND liquidity injected into the banking system will also be withdrawn unless the transactions are extended or replaced by other liquidity management instruments.
Overall, the central bank's stronger liquidity support could provide an additional tailwind for the stock market in the short term, particularly as investor sentiment shows signs of improvement.
However, for the VN-Index's recovery to become sustainable, the market will still need confirmation from the ability to maintain trading liquidity, the breadth of capital inflows and actual developments in interest rates in the coming period.
VN-Index rebounds nearly 2%, securities stocks lead gains
On the same day news emerged about the SBV's planned liquidity support, Vietnam's stock market staged a notable recovery on Wednesday. The VN-Index closed up 33.4 points, or 1.97%, at 1,733.02 points. The gain marked the benchmark's first advance after four consecutive losing sessions, allowing it to quickly reclaim the 1,700-point threshold breached in the previous session.
The recovery was broad-based and accompanied by a significant improvement in market liquidity. Trading volume on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HoSE) reached approximately 908.59 million shares, with a total transaction value of VND17,955 billion ($699.11 million), up 45.5% and nearly 38.8%, respectively, from the previous session.
Securities stocks were particularly prominent, attracting strong investor inflows, with several major stocks posting sharp gains. VCK rose 6.43%, TCX gained 6.98%, VND advanced 6.90%, VCI climbed 6.86%, VIX added 6.78% and SSI increased 6.53%. On the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX), MBS and SHS also surged by more than 7%.
Gains also spread to banking and real estate stocks. VPB rose 4.48%, CTG gained 3.33% and VCB advanced 2.43%. In the real estate sector, VHM climbed 2.10%, DXG jumped 6.57% and TCH surged 6.69%.
The market performance pointed to a significant improvement in buying demand and investor sentiment following a series of correction sessions. Financial and real estate stocks, which are particularly sensitive to interest rate movements, were also among the best-performing sectors.

articles.title: Govt urges expansion of intermediate manufacturing sector - ANTARA News
articles.summary: Govt urges expansion of intermediate manufacturing sector  ANTARA News
articles.full_text:
Industry Minister Muhammad Sarmuji (center), accompanied by the ministry's Director General of Small, Medium and Varied Industries Reni Yanita (right), inspects products on display at the Krista Interfood Exhibition and Indonesia Food Innovation (IFI) 2026 Awards in Tangerang, on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). (ANTARA/HO-Industry Ministry)
Speaking at the Indonesia Food Innovation Awards in Tangerang, Sarmuji emphasized that expanding intermediate processing enables domestic enterprises to move beyond basic consumer retail and integrate deeper into corporate supply chains.
"Intermediate products enable food businesses to take a broader role in the value chain—not only selling final products to consumers, but also supplying needs for other businesses and industries," Sarmuji said.
Highlighting innovations including sago- and cassava-based noodles, algae extracts, and fish-collagen processing, Sarmuji noted that utilizing agricultural and marine by-products supports circular economy goals while creating high-value opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises.
The food and beverage sector remains a cornerstone of Indonesia’s non-oil processing economy.
In the first half of 2026, the sector grew 6.77 percent, contributing 41.86 percent to non-oil manufacturing GDP.
Realized investment hit 47.74 trillion rupiah ($2.64 billion), with domestic capital accounting for 59 percent.
Between January and August 2026, food and beverage exports reached $34.65 billion against $9.7 billion in imports, generating a trade surplus of nearly $25 billion and employing approximately 6.9 million workers.
Sarmuji noted that national manufacturing momentum remains strong, with Indonesia’s Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rising to 54.0 in October 2026, outpacing regional peers including Japan, Vietnam, China, and South Korea.
Beyond food processing, the minister advocated leveraging local biodiversity for pharmaceutical raw materials to reduce import reliance, while utilizing Indonesian culinary exports as tools for soft diplomacy abroad.

articles.title: JB developer ordered to pay US$2.58 million to condo owners, including Singaporeans, over delays - CNA
articles.summary: JB developer ordered to pay US$2.58 million to condo owners, including Singaporeans, over delays  CNA
articles.full_text:
The owners of 84 units in R&F Princess Cove, a waterfront development overlooking the Woodlands Causeway, were awarded compensation for delays involving their units and shared facilities. The developer intends to appeal the decision, its lawyer told CNA.
JOHOR BAHRU: The developer of a high-end Johor Bahru condominium has been ordered to pay RM10.56 million (US$2.58 million) in compensation to a group of property owners, including Singaporeans, over delays in completing the project.
The Johor Bahru High Court ruled in favour of claims involving 84 condominium units in Princess Cove, finding that the developer, R&F Development Sdn Bhd, had breached its agreements with buyers by splitting the original first phase of the project into two.
This meant some buyers received their keys while parts of the sprawling development, including some shared facilities, were still unfinished.
The court, however, dismissed claims involving another 39 units, ordering the unsuccessful buyers to pay RM10,000 (US$2,454) in legal costs per unit to R&F. These buyers had signed their purchase agreements after the developer changed the building plans, according to lawyers involved in the case.
R&F's lawyer Josiah Tea told CNA the developer intends to appeal the ruling, which the purchasers’ lawyer and a property observer say underscore the importance of developers honouring the terms of their agreements with buyers, and will prove instructive for prospective buyers of Johor Bahru property.
Some successful claimants told CNA they were relieved by the outcome after a years-long legal battle. They said parts of the development were still under construction when they received their keys, affecting their experience living there.
R&F Princess Cove is a sprawling waterfront residential and commercial development in the heart of Johor Bahru, located adjacent to the Johor-Singapore Causeway.
Developed by China's R&F Group, Princess Cove’s proximity to Singapore is a key selling point, with a 650m covered pedestrian bridge connecting the development directly to Johor Bahru's Customs, Immigration and Quarantine complex.
According to a draft court order seen by CNA, the dispute centred on R&F's decision to divide the original first phase of the development into two separate phases, known as Phase 1A and Phase 1B.
Buyers of units in three residential blocks – A1, A2 and A7 – received their keys on Oct 25, 2017, but the original Phase 1 development was only completed in November 2018.
The court ruled that because R&F had breached the purchase agreements by splitting Phase 1 into two, November 2018 should be treated as the relevant handover date instead of October 2017.
This meant that although buyers received their units in 2017, the developer was only considered to have fulfilled its handover obligations in November 2018. The later date was then used to calculate the compensation for late delivery.
The court ordered R&F to compensate buyers of the 84 units for delays involving both their units and shared facilities.
Compensation was calculated at 10 per cent a year of each property's purchase price, while compensation for shared facilities was calculated at 10 per cent a year of one-fifth of the purchase price.
The buyers were awarded roughly RM34,000 to RM196,000 per unit for late delivery, and an additional RM6,900 to RM39,000 for delays in the completion of shared facilities.
R&F was also ordered to refund their maintenance fees, sinking fund contributions and water deposits collected before Nov 8, 2018.
The buyers were represented by lawyers NG Vinod and Rashmeet Kaur, while Josiah Tea and V Mavin Rajah represented R&F Development.
Vinod told CNA that his clients whose claims were dismissed intend to appeal the decision.
"LIVING IN A CONSTRUCTION SITE"
One of the successful claimants was Crystal Ng, a 49-year-old Singaporean who has since sold her family's unit, saying the experience left "a sour taste".
"When we received keys to the unit (in October 2017), the whole area was very messy and full of construction debris. Even the access route to our block was still obstructed … there was a fence erected on the road," said Ng, who is semi-retired.
The 18th-floor unit was purchased under her mother's name.
The lawsuit, involving 145 named plaintiffs, was filed in 2019.
In 2021, the purchasers initially secured a court ruling in their favour without a full trial.
However, R&F successfully appealed that decision, leading to a 10-day trial that concluded in 2024. The latest ruling was delivered on Sep 10, 2026.
Ng said the prolonged fight had been worthwhile because it allowed the owners to pursue their claims collectively.
"When we purchase a unit, we expect the developer to fulfill its obligation. So what should be an exciting milestone for us became a prolonged and painful ordeal," she said.
Another Singaporean, Hong Wei Zhong, 45, said the condominium's facilities, including swimming pools, were not ready when his family received the keys in October 2017.
Hong, a manager whose family purchased a 10th-floor unit under his mother's name, said the experience felt like "living in a construction site".
"I tried to engage the developer directly but then (it) refused to entertain us. At that point, I decided to speak with other owners in person and through Facebook and see if we can collectively engage a lawyer to file a lawsuit," he said.
Hong's mother is among those successful in seeking damages from the developer.
Hong told CNA that if the appeal involving the 39 units is unsuccessful, the successful claimants plan to pool part of their compensation to cover the legal costs payable to the developer.
Lawyer Rajah, who represented R&F Development, told CNA that the developer disputed some of the purchasers' complaints about the condominium's facilities.
He cited a claim by some purchasers that the squash court did not meet the dimensions of an Olympic-sized court, describing it as "ridiculous".
"Are you saying that just because one or two facilities which could not be used entitles you to say that (you) don't want to pay for maintenance fees?" he said.
“Our position was that although some facilities were not available at the time, there were still other facilities (in operation)," he added.
In a separate lawsuit filed in February 2023, 167 R&F Princess Cove owners took legal action against the developer over delays in obtaining strata titles for their units.
According to a Free Malaysia Today report, the court ruled in favour of the owners and awarded them RM10,000 in legal costs.
However, the court did not award damages, noting that the strata titles had since been issued.
WHAT THE RULING MEANS FOR PROPERTY BUYERS
Johor-based property consultant Samuel Tan said handing over keys while parts of a development remain under construction could affect buyers' quality of life and potentially hurt rental returns and property values.
"If common facilities, lifts, fire safety systems or access roads are incomplete, the property is functionally unliveable," said Tan, chief executive of Olive Tree Property Consultants.
"Winning compensation not just for late housing units, but separately for the delayed completion of common facilities and infrastructure, reinforces that a condo is not delivered merely when four concrete walls are standing. Liveability is tied to the wider ecosystem promised in the marketing and sales pitch," he said.
Tan added that the dismissal of the other purchasers' claims showed why buyers should pay close attention to the terms of their agreements, particularly if a developer has already made changes to a project's plans.
"If you buy into a project after a plan modification has already been formally integrated, claiming ignorance later becomes legally difficult," he said.
Lawyer Vinod, who represented the purchasers, advised prospective foreign buyers in Johor to research a developer's track record and carefully review their sale and purchase agreements before committing to a property.
"Buyers often rely on what the marketing person told them during the launch or the sales promotion, and they don't realise that whatever that was claimed or promoted, if it is not in the sale and purchase agreement, then the developer is not duty-bound to deliver," he told CNA.
Vinod also advised buyers to inspect their properties carefully during the handover, preferably together with a representative of the developer, and to ensure any defects are recorded for rectification.
"If these issues are paid attention to, then I think they shouldn't have any problems," Vinod said.

articles.title: Korea Deep Learning Tests AI Agent With Shinhan Vietnam Finance - Seoul Economic Daily
articles.summary: Korea Deep Learning Tests AI Agent With Shinhan Vietnam Finance  Seoul Economic Daily
articles.full_text:
Korea Deep Learning, an artificial intelligence startup, said on the 5th that it had completed a proof-of-concept test of financial task automation technology with Shinhan Vietnam Finance Co. (SVFC) through Shinhan Futures Lab Vietnam, Shinhan Financial Group's global startup incubation platform.
The test was carried out as part of a global open innovation project hosted and organized by Shinhan Bank Vietnam and the Seoul Business Agency (SBA). The program connects South Korean startups with Vietnamese financial institutions to validate technologies needed for local financial operations.
Korea Deep Learning used Deep Agent, its in-house AI task automation solution, for the test. Deep Agent runs on Deep OCR, which recognizes and extracts required information from documents, and Deep Parser, which analyzes document structure and organizes the data. The test examined whether the system could extract and organize document data required for financial operations in Vietnam and link that output to downstream task automation. The results earned the company the Global Shinhan InnoBoost Open Innovation Reward.
The company plans to use the test as a springboard to expand into overseas financial markets, including Vietnam. It will develop solutions tailored to the operating environments of local financial institutions and increase cooperation with overseas companies. It also plans to broaden the application of its AI task automation technology beyond finance into a range of other industries.
"We showed the capability to connect information recognition and data processing technology to actual task automation," said Kim Dong-hyun, chief strategy officer at Korea Deep Learning. "We expect this achievement to further expand our business opportunities in the global market."
